source_review.notes: Checked all seven official/primary sources. Current gRPC deadline and cancellation guides support explicit realistic deadlines, DEADLINE_EXCEEDED/cancellation behavior, remaining-time propagation, clock-skew mitigation, and application responsibility to stop spawned work. AWS Builders' Library supports latency-distribution/false-timeout selection, connection/TLS coverage, retries/backoff/jitter, and deployment/cold-connection concerns. Google SRE chapters support user-facing SLO distributions, deadline/cancellation cascading-failure controls, retry amplification, and bimodal in-flight resource examples. Current OpenTelemetry RPC span conventions support RPC method/status/error telemetry while the chapter labels application budget fields as locally governed additions. RFC 9110 is used only for HTTP semantic context.

evidence: Checked deadline D, monotonic time t, reserve r, budget B(t), serial caps b_i, parallel times p_j, queue q, work floor w_min, arrival lambda, time W, and in-flight L for consistent units/domains.
Confirmed remaining budget is clamped nonnegative and recomputed rather than restarted.
Confirmed serial latency sums while parallel critical latency uses maximum plus joins, even though parallel resource work sums.
notation_and_syntax.notes: SLO distributions, request deadlines, phase timeouts, message expiry, and leases remain separate time concepts.

evidence: Recomputed checkout allocation as 100+250+220+350+100+80+100=1,200 ms.
Recomputed mixture mean as 0.97*0.08+0.03*20=0.6776 s and Little's Law as 2,400*0.6776=1,626.24 in-flight.
Recomputed two-second stalled deadline as mean 0.1376 s and 330.24 in-flight, a reduction of 1,296.
Recomputed 20 independent 1%-slow branches as 1-0.99^20=0.18209, about 18.2% at least one slow.
Recomputed 5% of 1,000 QPS stalled for 100 seconds as 50*100=5,000 concurrent stalled requests; counted ten examples/five answer pairs.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All numeric scenarios declare simplifying independence/stability assumptions and require measured production validation.

evidence: Constructed three-hop reset-timeout trace showing end-to-end duration can exceed caller intent, while remaining-time propagation prevents reset.
Confirmed admission floor plus final reserve rejects work that cannot return before deadline.
Constructed fan-out quorum trace showing cancellation of losers reduces resource work without changing completed result semantics.
Constructed cancellation-versus-commit interleavings showing timeout cannot prove absence of effect.
Confirmed retry feasibility requires remaining time for backoff, useful attempt, and final response under one parent deadline.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Resource-residence bound depends on actual cooperative cancellation latency and separately durable workflows are explicit exceptions.

evidence: Reviewed absent/zero/negative/huge/overflow/rounded deadlines, wall-clock skew, monotonic elapsed time, proxy metadata loss/reset, and untrusted client clamps.
Reviewed DNS/pool/connect/TLS/upload/headers/body/idle, queue/admission, fan-out/join, lock/statement/transaction/commit, retry/hedge, cleanup, stream, and async-workflow boundaries.

Reviewed caller disconnect, fatal sibling, cancellation/completion race, ignored cancellation, stale commit, timeout-after-external-success, same/new effect ID, deadline/TTL/lease/redrive, and failover.
Reviewed saturation, bimodal tails, hot tenants, cold deployment, nested retries, high-cardinality/sensitive timing metadata, and misleading censored latency.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Coverage spans every waiting/execution/effect phase plus overload, clock, streaming, asynchronous, and adversarial inputs.

evidence: Confirmed every child/attempt deadline is no later than current parent remaining time and includes future response reserve.
Confirmed expired/impossible/overloaded work is rejected before scarce allocation and queues/tenants are bounded.
Confirmed cancellation reaches child RPCs, tasks, queries, hedges, streams, and safe cleanup while fenced commits reject stale workers.
Confirmed retries preserve operation/effect ID and timeout ambiguity uses status query/ledger/reconciliation.
Confirmed long workflows transfer ownership durably with separate workflow deadlines rather than detach request work invisibly.
invariant_checking.notes: The chapter never treats cancellation as rollback or deadline exceeded as proof of failure.

evidence: Reviewed remaining-budget proof and confirmed monotonic deduction, child cap, admission floor, cancellation observation, and bounded cleanup assumptions are necessary.
Reviewed Little's Law use and confirmed it is labeled stable-system planning, not a transient saturation theorem.
Reviewed SLO-versus-timeout argument and confirmed timeout-censored successful latency cannot independently select a safe cutoff.
Reviewed database/provider ambiguity argument and confirmed identity/outcome participation is required beyond time control.
proof_review.notes: Timeouts bound waiting/resource exposure; they do not create transactional certainty.

evidence: Confirmed proof sketch states its conclusion and explicit effect-ambiguity limitation.
Confirmed gRPC, AWS, Google SRE, OpenTelemetry, and HTTP behavior/guidance is attributed rather than generalized as one protocol.
Confirmed product/library facts, architecture recommendations, statistical models, and empirical obligations remain distinct.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Library defaults and phase coverage are explicitly retrieval/test obligations.

evidence: All seven primary sources were retrieved or checked on 2026-09-02 where current documentation applies.
All deadlines, percentiles, probabilities, QPS, branch counts, worker counts, and phase allocations are labeled examples/exercises.

Actual user abandonment, phase distributions, false-timeout rate, cancellation latency, driver/query behavior, safe floors, retry/hedge load, stream behavior, SLO/error budget, and ambiguous-effect recovery remain explicit load/integration/fault evidence obligations.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No production client, proxy, service, database, provider, or workload was empirically assessed.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed time-concept separation, user/SLO basis, remaining-budget computation, serial/parallel allocation, client phases, queue/admission, database resources, cancellation, retry/hedge, async boundaries, response semantics, observability, and fault verification as one end-to-end model.

practitioner_review.notes: Checked implementability through workload classes, measured phase histograms, deadline clamps/propagation, stage caps/floors/reserves, bounded queues/fan-out/pools/locks/streams, database server timeouts, cooperative child cancellation, same-ID reconciliation, async operation state, typed errors, tracing, fake-clock tests, and tail-load fault injection.

pedagogical_review.notes: The module starts by separating commonly conflated time concepts, derives budgets over critical paths, then applies them to phases, queues, databases, cancellation, retries, asynchronous work, and observability. Ten examples isolate failure surfaces; five exercises progress from allocation and arithmetic to writes, fan-out, and full-stack verification with complete answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
